title: Daniel Guetta on the Guts of AI, Agentic AI & Why LLMs Hallucinate | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 46

metadata.title: Daniel Guetta on the Guts of AI, Agentic AI & Why LLMs Hallucinate | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 46
metadata.transcript_type: publisher machine transcript with speaker markers

transcript_hash_basis: Normalized source metadata records the underlying full transcript hash. All normalized segments were read.
summary: Eisman seeks a second technical view after Gary Marcus. Guetta argues that imperfect present-day AI can create value through representations, retrieval and tools without resolving AGI. The interview contains useful deployment distinctions, but its repeated full-context-recomputation and nearest-word explanations are technically misleading. Eisman leaves the industry return-on-investment verdict open until 2027-2028.
assessment: Empirical premises and forecasts are assessed separately. Guest assertions are not Eisman forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal attribution remain unresolved.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Columbia professor Daniel Guetta. Guest technical assertions and personal coding-view revisions remain guest claims. The host's acceptance of the inference-energy explanation is recorded separately.
framework_points: Separate useful task economics from claims of general intelligence.
Benchmark performance is specific to a task distribution.
Data access, integration and action controls are deployment requirements.
Lower coding cost does not automatically erase workflow and coordination moats.
Use explicit cost and error budgets to evaluate imperfect tools.
Eisman actively seeks a competing expert view and retains a 2027-2028 ROI horizon.
tools_and_charts: Learned embeddings and the Transformer architecture.
KV caching as a correction to the inference-cost explanation.
Reinforcement learning with human feedback and verifiable rewards.
transcript_cautions: Every one of the 1,293 supplied normalized segments was read in full.

The supplied publisher transcript contains repeated watermark-like lines and multi-second gaps, including parts of the travel and database examples and the closing disruption discussion. Read-complete refers to all available text, not a claim of complete audio recovery.
SPEAKER_01 generally identifies Eisman and SPEAKER_02 Guetta, with occasional joined turns; the disclaimer is SPEAKER_00.
The host describes Marcus's views to elicit a second opinion; they are not automatically Eisman predictions.
Guetta qualifies his AGI skepticism and explicitly disclaims expertise about several markets; the host's closing summary is stronger than the guest's actual language.
The old 5% enterprise-readiness estimate is explicitly described by the guest as outdated.
materiality_note: Major investment theses are distinguished from supporting factual premises. No overall accuracy percentage is appropriate.
